Not OP, but I figured I'd answer anyways as I share a similar viewpoint.

  1. Current governments solved the problems they were created to solve. We aren't subjects of a monarch anymore, we aren't usually taxed without voting on it or voting in the people who made the decisions, we have religious freedom to a degree unimagined in the 1700s. However, the new system most definitely generated new problems as well. The next iteration should be designed to address both problem sets. As for why government, the concept of a government is the only thing which is supposed to solely represent the interests of it's people (companies have profits, NGOs have to worry about getting the next round of donations, etc).

  2. If you are rational about the nature of man, we're all the same except a few minor genetic flukes and societal differentiation. Thus, everyone should be able to be governed in the same way, providing minor exceptions for personality. As for why, the fact of the matter is that the true barriers and 'enemies' of people don't lie on this planet. They are asteroids, and the vacuum of space, and solar flares that could knock out whole hemisphere's electricity... The sooner we stop our in-fighting and face those oppponents the better, and the more assured our species's survival is.

  3. Wealth is a funny thing. You will find many different ideas about the way future economic systems should be designed. Some argue the most cut-throat anarcho-capitalism, while others argue for a self-organizing commons. Still others have even weirder ideas, not to mention all of the potential ways to represent currency in the digital age and what it's basis should be. I don't think anyone will know what will actually work until we have tried a number of systems. The best thing to do would be to have several different economic systems running at the same time and allow them to compete by whom participates in which.

  4. Arguably wars, at least large total-conflict wars, are on a decline. That still doesn't prevent any number of conflicts, scirmishes, civil wars and unrecognized rebellions from happening at any point in time in our modern world. And I think a return of total war is inevitable at some point in the future. It will probably look as different from WWII as WWII did from the civil war, but it will be a large war, and it will be for 'keeps'. The only way to even attempt to stop that cycle at some point in the future is to get everyone fighting against something larger than the world (preferably an inanimate object or event).
